newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFIs ready to seek public trade approval.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFIs ready to seek public trade approval.

text.p: The Polish Treasury Ministry hopes to submit issue prospectuses of all 15 National Investment Funds (NFIs) to the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) by mid-December, a deputy minister said on Tuesday.
Wieslaw Kaczmarek told a news briefing the ministry expected to complete its review of the first prospectus and submit it for approval for public trade as early as this week.
"It is possible that we will submit the first issue prospectus this week... I would like to see all NFI issue prospectuses submitted to the KPW by mid-December," Kaczmarek said.

He said that all 15 funds, which control 512 companies under the country's mass privatisation scheme, had completed work on their issue prospectuses and the ministry hoped the commission would manage to clear the funds for public trade by early March 1997.
Kaczmarek also confirmed that the ministry would not grant an extension of the November 22 deadline by which 28 million adult Poles could pick up participation units in the programme.
By the end of last week about 24 million Poles had subscribed to the certificates and Kaczmarek said he expected the final figure to exceed 25 million.
The certificates will later be exchangeable for 15 shares, one share in each fund, due to be listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange in the second quarter of next year.
